AUDIT: FAIL
Objective Understood: Reviewed worker task 'Close a real fabrication loophole, not_applicable_confirmed must come from a real re-runnable audit script, never an AI narrative' (risk tier: tier1) by reading the actual diff, not a self-report.
Standards Reviewed: AGENTS.md Operating Rule 7c structured audit protocol; risk-tier.py's deterministic tier classification.
Scope Confirmed:  ...UTION_AND_MERGE_SAFETY_CORRECTION_2026-08-05.md |  66 +++++
 PROGRESS.md                                        | 157 +++++------
 audit_ocid_canonical_registry.py                   | 297 +++++++++++++++++----
 tests/test_audit_ocid_canonical_registry.py        | 155 ++++++++++-
 4 files changed, 517 insertions(+), 158 deletions(-)
Evidence Recorded: The intent and most of the mechanics of this diff are sound (a real deterministic char cap on oversized evidence leaves, and a merge rule that now always preserves existing canonical_umr_id/status/all_umr_ids/pr_number/pr_repo/not_found instead of silently overwriting them), and the full 116-test suite passes; however, live reproduction of the new plan_for_ocid()/main() code path against a seeded row shows a confirmed severe regression: main()'s --apply call to upsert_ocid_canonical_registry() only passes canonical_umr_id/status/all_umr_ids/evidence/pr_number/pr_repo/duplicate_reason/not_found/audit_raw_output, never the plan's existing commit_sha/file_name/file_path/merge_status/evidence_summary -- so upsert's ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE unconditionally sets those five columns to their unpassed defaults (NULL) via excluded.*, silently wiping out the real per-OCID backfill data just landed in PR #64 (49/69 commit_sha, 23/69 file_path, 57/69 merge_status, 69/69 evidence_summary) for every one of the 69 existing rows the very next time --apply runs -- which this same PR's own PROGRESS.md lists as its next queued action. This is exactly the class of silent, live-data-destroying overwrite this task's own stated mission is to eliminate, it is not covered by any of the new or existing tests (none of which seed/assert on commit_sha/file_name/file_path/merge_status/evidence_summary through plan_for_ocid()->upsert), and it was independently reproduced live in this review (before/after row dump) rather than inferred from the diff alone. Separately, the PR's own new addendum doc ships with literal 'TBD' placeholders for its claimed live-apply results and PROGRESS.md's own Remaining section still lists the live re-run and independent review as outstanding, so this diff is not actually ready to represent itself as a completed, verified task even setting the bug aside. Issues found: CONFIRMED (live-reproduced): audit_ocid_canonical_registry.py main()'s --apply path calls sbr.upsert_ocid_canonical_registry() without commit_sha/file_name/file_path/merge_status/evidence_summary, so upsert's ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE overwrites those 5 real, previously-backfilled columns to NULL on every existing row touched -- silent production data loss on the very next --apply run, which PROGRESS.md lists as this task's next step. plan_for_ocid() must carry these fields from `existing` into the plan, and main() must pass them through to upsert_ocid_canonical_registry(), with a regression test asserting they survive a preserve-path re-audit.; Do not run audit_ocid_canonical_registry.py --apply against the live production DB until the above is fixed -- it will destroy the OCID-068 Phase 2 dedicated-column backfill from PR #64.; OCID_068_PHASE_2_LIVE_REAUDIT_EXECUTION_AND_MERGE_SAFETY_CORRECTION_2026-08-05.md ships with unresolved 'TBD' placeholders for its own claimed live-apply results, and PROGRESS.md's Remaining section still lists the live re-run, post-apply confirmation, and independent review as outstanding -- this diff documents itself as work-in-progress, not a completed task ready to merge as done.; Minor, non-blocking: _bounded_for_storage()'s idempotence check (`_TRUNCATION_MARKER_SENTINEL in value`) skips capping any oversized string that happens to already contain that literal marker substring, even if it did not come from a prior truncation -- low real-world likelihood but not structurally impossible.
Severity Classified: medium
Verdict: fail
Corrective Action Owner: Worker to address the findings listed above and resubmit.
Re-Audit Scheduled: Required after corrective changes are pushed.

AUDIT: FAIL
Objective Understood: Reviewed worker task 'Reconcile UMR-20260805-092408-4f97: PR72 fresh AUDIT:FAIL, re-review (non-mechanical fix, needs real worker pass)' (risk tier: tier1) by reading the actual diff, not a self-report.
Standards Reviewed: AGENTS.md Operating Rule 7c structured audit protocol; risk-tier.py's deterministic tier classification.
Scope Confirmed:  ...UTION_AND_MERGE_SAFETY_CORRECTION_2026-08-05.md |  66 +++++
 PROGRESS.md                                        | 157 +++++------
 audit_ocid_canonical_registry.py                   | 297 +++++++++++++++++----
 tests/test_audit_ocid_canonical_registry.py        | 155 ++++++++++-
 4 files changed, 517 insertions(+), 158 deletions(-)
Evidence Recorded: The code change itself is sound: plan_for_ocid()'s merge-rule rewrite genuinely fixes a real silent-overwrite risk (existing canonical_umr_id/status/all_umr_ids/pr_number/pr_repo/not_found are now always preserved, with disagreements appended once as an idempotent NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW note) and _bounded_for_storage() correctly caps oversized evidence leaves before storage; I independently ran the full test suite (116/116 passed, including all 6 tests in the touched test file) rather than trusting the self-report, and no .github/workflows/**, migration/schema/auth/security-path files are touched, so tier1 classification is correct. However, the PR's own artifacts show the task is not actually finished: the new addendum doc's 'Real live-apply results' section is explicitly left as TBD ('FILLED IN AFTER THE LIVE RUN COMPLETES'), the tip commit message itself says 'results TBD, filling in after live --apply completes', and PROGRESS.md's Remaining checklist still lists re-running the live --apply across all 69 OCIDs, confirming post-apply state, spot-checking DB size delta, independent review, and opening the final PR as unchecked. The one thing this task was dispatched to actually do -- execute and verify the corrected script against live production data -- is undocumented as done, so the corrected merge-safety logic remains unproven against the real data it was built to protect. Recommend the worker complete the live --apply, fill in real results, verify no existing canonical rows were disturbed, and resubmit. Issues found: Addendum doc (OCID_068_PHASE_2_LIVE_REAUDIT_EXECUTION_AND_MERGE_SAFETY_CORRECTION_2026-08-05.md) leaves 'Real live-apply results' as TBD placeholders -- the live production --apply this task exists to perform was never confirmed complete.; PROGRESS.md's own 'Remaining' section lists unresolved items (re-run live --apply, confirm post-apply state, spot-check DB size delta, independent review, final commit+push+PR) -- this diff reads as a mid-task WIP snapshot, not completed work ready for autonomous merge.; No workflow-file (.github/workflows/**) changes present in this diff -- hard rule not implicated.
Severity Classified: medium
Verdict: fail
Corrective Action Owner: Worker to address the findings listed above and resubmit.
Re-Audit Scheduled: Required after corrective changes are pushed.

AUDIT: FAIL
Objective Understood: Reviewed worker task 'sweep-adopt-veridian-scripts-72-close-a-real-fabrication-loophole-not-ap' (risk tier: tier1) by reading the actual diff, not a self-report.
Standards Reviewed: AGENTS.md Operating Rule 7c structured audit protocol; risk-tier.py's deterministic tier classification.
Scope Confirmed:  ...UTION_AND_MERGE_SAFETY_CORRECTION_2026-08-05.md |  66 +++++
 PROGRESS.md                                        | 157 +++++------
 audit_ocid_canonical_registry.py                   | 297 +++++++++++++++++----
 tests/test_audit_ocid_canonical_registry.py        | 155 ++++++++++-
 4 files changed, 517 insertions(+), 158 deletions(-)
Evidence Recorded: The core code change (audit_ocid_canonical_registry.py's _bounded_for_storage() cap and the plan_for_ocid() merge-rule rewrite that now always preserves an existing row's canonical_umr_id/status/all_umr_ids/pr_number/pr_repo/not_found instead of letting a spurious full-text match silently overwrite it) is a real, well-reasoned, well-tested fix -- I traced the old vs. new logic by hand and the described OCID-001/OCID-007/OCID-011 overwrite bugs are genuine given the prior code, and the new tests (bounding determinism/idempotence, preserve-and-flag-for-review, idempotent NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW note, end-to-end bounded write) correctly exercise the fixed behavior. However, the task's own artifacts show this submission is not actually finished: the new OCID_068_PHASE_2_LIVE_REAUDIT_... addendum has every real-outcome field left as literal 'TBD' (OCIDs re-audited, rows preserved, rows flagged for review, DB size delta), and PROGRESS.md's own 'Remaining' section still lists re-running the live --apply, confirming post-apply results, spot-checking the DB size delta, independent review before merge, and even 'Final commit + push, open PR' as not done. A diff that self-documents its central deliverable (the live production re-audit run and its verification) as not yet performed is not ready for autonomous tier1 merge regardless of how sound the code itself looks; merging now would close out a task the worker's own record says is still in progress. Issues found: OCID_068_PHASE_2_LIVE_REAUDIT_EXECUTION_AND_MERGE_SAFETY_CORRECTION_2026-08-05.md's 'Real live-apply results' section is entirely 'TBD' placeholders -- the live --apply against production (the task's stated primary deliverable) is not confirmed to have actually run or produced verified results.; PROGRESS.md's own 'Remaining' checklist still lists re-running the live --apply, confirming post-apply gate outcomes, spot-checking DB size delta, independent review before merge, and opening the PR as not yet done -- this diff appears to be a mid-task WIP snapshot, not a completed task ready for autonomous merge.; Minor, non-blocking: the NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW note-append guard only checks for the sentinel's presence, not whether corroboration was later restored, so a stale review note could persist indefinitely across future re-runs even after a human resolves the disagreement -- worth a follow-up but not a reason to hold this diff on its own.
Severity Classified: medium
Verdict: fail
Corrective Action Owner: Worker to address the findings listed above and resubmit.
Re-Audit Scheduled: Required after corrective changes are pushed.
